messages:
maya (PM): quick sync — sketching the next milestone for Dedicated capacity. need to lock autoscale hysteresis, burst semantics, and the fairness fallback behavior before we freeze scope for Q2.

eric (Eng): +1. two engineering constraints: 1) autoscale decision must be stable over short spikes (avoid flip-flop), 2) quota checks need microsecond budget in hot path.

satya (SRE): for stability we recommend a two-tier hysteresis: short window (30s) for fast scaling + long cooldown (10m) to avoid thrash. also prewarm pipeline to reduce cold-kernel penalties.

maya (PM): that sounds sensible. proposal: autoscale policy = threshold-based ingress + exponential backoff for scale-down. documentable knobs: scale-up aggressiveness, scale-down cooldown, prewarm headroom.

eric (Eng): implementation sketch: maintain per-pool moving percentiles (p50,p95,p99) and an exponential moving average for request rate. if p95 > threshold && rate rising -> trigger scale-up. scale-down only if both p95 below lower-bound AND rate decays by >30% for cooldown window.

lee (Product Ops): console needs to show these knobs with sensible defaults; non-engineering users want "Burst buffer" slider + "Fairness mode" toggle. also, add tooltip: what happens when fairness mode is ON (weighted sharing vs first-come).

angela (Sales): enterprise asks: their critical flows must not see >20% latency regression during bursts. they'd accept paid-prewarm add-on. can we offer a "Guaranteed burst" SKU for top-tier customers?

maya (PM): we can. plan: MVP includes a paid prewarm option that reserves ephemeral warm slots during customer window. hard guarantees come later if legal OKs SLA wording.

metricsbot: Synthetic test 2026-05-01T12:15Z: 10k rps mixed; p95 delta with prewarm=+4%, without prewarm=+18%; spillover count (no prewarm)=2.3% of requests.

eric (Eng): nice numbers. question: how do we account for fairness during congestion? options: weighted fairshare by committed capacity, or proportional token burn. my vote: proportional token burn (simpler runtime).

satya (SRE): proportional token burn is operationally easier but can be surprising to customers. fairshare by committed weight aligns with contracts. maybe both: default proportional, enterprise toggle to strict-weighted.

maya (PM): compromise accepted. feature matrix: default proportional fallback; premium: weighted fairshare + guaranteed burst SKU.

eric (Eng): telemetry requirements (to wire into autoscale): need stream of per-pool metrics: pool_id, committed_capacity, inflight_requests, p50/p95/p99_latency, token_burn_rate, prewarm_slots_used, eviction_reason, timestamp.

lee (Product Ops): UI telemetry: show predicted time-to-scale and current headroom. also surface "likely-impact" score for admins when they change knobs.

angela (Sales): for billing: record "burst_consumed" per charge window and surface an invoice line. customers expect clear math: burst token price or hourly prewarm fee.

maya (PM): launch gates proposal: 1) perf canary: p95 token latency delta < 10% for 48h on staging replay; 2) fairness smoke: under synthetic congestion, premium-weighted mode never reduces committed-customer throughput below 95% of baseline; 3) billing: invoice preview for burst month and legal signoff on "guaranteed burst" language.

eric (Eng): canary plan: run proportional fallback by default, enable weighted mode behind flag for 2 enterprise tenants. collect comparison.

satya (SRE): ops runbook items: automated drain + reclaim sequence, customer-notify template, escalation path when prewarm exhaustion occurs. owner: @satya by 2026-04-20.

eric (Eng): infra owners: autoscale controller core - me, prewarm pipeline - @eric_helper, quota fast-path - @kim. target PRs by 2026-04-15.

lee (Product Ops): docs owner: @lee will draft console copy and admin tooltips by 2026-04-18.

angela (Sales): sales/finance owner: @angela to propose burst pricing tiers and invoice examples by 2026-04-22.

maya (PM): risks: 1) autoscale overshoot causing cost spike; 2) customer surprise from proportional burn; 3) telemetry gaps for fast incidents. mitigations: spend 2 sprints on tuning + run a cross-team dry-run.

eric (Eng): mitigation detail: include an autoscale budget cap per-pool to limit cost during experiments.

satya (SRE): also add a safety circuit: if cluster-wide GPU utilization > 85% then automatically throttle non-committed burst usage.

maya (PM): good. next steps: Eric posts design doc + traffic model, Satya posts runbook draft, Lee shares UI mocks. sync Friday 9am PT.

eric (Eng): doc link: https://docs.internal/r/redwood/dedicated/autoscale-hysteresis-draft (will push by EOD).

satya (SRE): runbook draft at https://wiki.internal/prewarm-runbook (linking in thread after upload).

maya (PM): thumbs: ship MVP with proportional fallback + paid prewarm, gated weighted fairshare behind enterprise toggle?

eric (Eng): :thumbsup:

satya (SRE): :thumbsup:

angela (Sales): :thumbsup: (need to talk to two accounts about prewarm pricing)

metricsbot: Thread archived by system after 14 days of inactivity.
